title: Steering Multirobot Behavior via Closed-Loop Affine Activation Editing
models: decentralized end-to-end RL multi-quadrotor navigation policy (QuadSwarm; MLP encoders + multi-head attention + MLP thrust head)
distilled diffusion policy (only for the DSRL comparison)
action_head: regression head (four normalized rotor thrusts); not a foundation model
methods: sparse autoencoder on a 30-dim post-attention activation
split-stable Pearson probing of SAE latents against rollout metrics to pick behavior latents
Beta-PPO steering policy that outputs per-latent multiplicative gains and additive offsets each step
ablations: multiplicative-only, additive-only, full-activation editing, SAE reconstruction only, fine-tuning, from-scratch
question: Can a frozen multirobot policy be steered toward new behaviors (velocity tracking, formation, camera avoidance) by a learned closed-loop editor of a few SAE latents, without forgetting its navigation skill?
key_findings: Velocity tracking error 0.322 -> 0.085 m/s (about 3.8x); residual action RL with the same budget reaches 0.269; additive-only editing 0.129 but collision-free rate falls to 80.6%.
Formation error 0.280 -> 0.086 (about 3.2x) with 98.5% collision-free and 99.4% robot success; additive-only 0.096 but 76.4% CF and 81.4% success; residual action RL 0.247.

Stealth (camera exposure, a behavior absent from training): watchability 3596.6 -> 1151.3 with 96.5% CF and 91.2% success; additive-only 1261.0 with 45.8% CF; multiplicative-only reduces exposure about 4%.
Fixed-scalar SAE steering and linear-probe intervention baselines improve velocity tracking only marginally and struggle on formation.

SAE reconstruction alone leaves behavior at base level (formation error 0.284, CF 99.1%); editing all 30 raw activation dims instead of selected SAE latents gives formation error 0.797, CF 66.6%, success 0.127.
Fine-tuning the policy on the formation reward ends at formation error 0.199 with CF 93.5% (forgetting); training from scratch fails within the same budget.
Zero-shot hardware deployment on Crazyflie 2.1 (C on STM32, 100 Hz) for the formation task is shown qualitatively.

evidence.setting: both (simulation for all numbers; hardware qualitative only)
benchmarks: QuadSwarm, 8 quadrotors, 10x10x10 m room with obstacles
evidence.scale: 1,000 distinct environment configurations (seeds) per method per behavior; number of steering-policy training seeds not reported
evidence.statistics: no tests or CIs; means over 1,000 episodes; learning curves from 'representative runs'
evidence.baselines: frozen base policy, residual action RL, DSRL on a distilled diffusion policy, fixed-scalar SAE steering, linear-probe intervention, single-component ablations, fine-tuning, training from scratch

causal_validation: Edits are interventions by construction and the SAE-reconstruction control rules out an SAE-insertion artifact. But the latents are chosen by correlation and the editor is an RL policy optimized on the target reward, so the result shows controllability through a bottleneck, not that the selected latents mean what their probe labels say.
closed_loop: Yes, all metrics are closed-loop multi-agent rollouts; the editor itself is a closed-loop policy.
limitations_stated: Latent selection relies on rollout-derived metrics; for behaviors exogenous to the base objective, trajectory proxies were used.
No formal safety or stability guarantees for the edited system.
Not yet applied to large pretrained models such as VLAs.
critique: The policy is a small RL controller with a 30-dimensional intervention activation, so results say little about VLA-scale models, despite the 'core' tag; it belongs with methods that could later be ported.

CLAE is essentially an RL policy acting through a learned latent interface; the comparison with residual action RL at equal budget is the key evidence that the activation interface helps, and it is favourable, but only one training seed is implied.
Hardware result is qualitative, one task, no metrics.
Good ablation design (SAE-only, raw-activation editing, multiplicative vs additive) compared with most VLA steering papers.
code: project page https://clae-robotics.github.io/ (code status not stated)
one_line: A learned RL editor that rescales and shifts a few probe-selected SAE latents inside a frozen multi-quadrotor policy makes it track velocities, hold formations and avoid cameras while keeping its navigation skills, outperforming residual-action RL and fixed steering.
